- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — leading to overcorrection; dampen forecast slope after sharp rises.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been trending sharply upward for 5+ days, forecast should gradually slope downward unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts — especially if sentiment turns negative mid-horizon; adjust forecast downward if sentiment drops below 0.4 after day 10–15.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) over 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate; add 2–3% buffer to forecast to account for hidden support.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is inconsistent or mixed — model often overfits short-term momentum; use smoother trend filters.
